content.text: Now I'll run the main cohort analysis. This single query defines frequent exacerbators, assigns their index regimen (ICS-inclusive if any ICS present in the initiation window, else LABA/LAMA if both a LABA and LAMA present), and computes the 12-month post-index exacerbation-visit proportion.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH exac AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, co.condition_start_date AS ev_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (257004,4115044,44807895,46270376,40316540,4110056,46269701)
),
drugcls AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_exposure_start_date AS dt,
    CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (1149380,939259,1115572,905233) THEN 'ICS'
         WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (1106776,44785907,45775571,42873639) THEN 'LAMA'
         WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (1137529,1196677,43532539,45775116,40240664) THEN 'LABA'
    END AS cls
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (1149380,939259,1115572,905233,1106776,44785907,45775571,42873639,1137529,1196677,43532539,45775116,40240664)
),
idx AS (  -- first maintenance inhaler date per person (index)
  SELECT person_id, MIN(dt) AS index_date FROM drugcls GROUP BY person_id
),
regimen AS (  -- classes present within 90 days of index
  SELECT d.person_id, i.index_date,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.cls='ICS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_ics,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.cls='LABA' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_laba,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.cls='LAMA' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_lama
  FROM drugcls d JOIN idx i ON d.person_id = i.person_id
  WHERE d.dt >= i.index_date AND d.dt <= DATEADD(day,90,i.index_date)
  GROUP BY d.person_id, i.index_date
),
grp AS (
  SELECT person_id, index_date,
    CASE WHEN has_ics=1 THEN 'ICS-inclusive'
         WHEN has_laba=1 AND has_lama=1 THEN 'LABA/LAMA' END AS trt_group
  FROM regimen
),
freq AS (  -- >=2 exacerbations in 12 months before index
  SELECT g.person_id
  FROM grp g JOIN exac e ON e.person_id = g.person_id
  WHERE e.ev_date < g.index_date AND e.ev_date >= DATEADD(day,-365,g.index_date)
  GROUP BY g.person_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
SELECT g.trt_group,
  COUNT(DISTINCT g.person_id) AS n_patients,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e2.person_id IS NOT NULL THEN g.person_id END) AS n_with_post_exac
FROM grp g
JOIN freq f ON f.person_id = g.person_id
LEFT JOIN exac e2 ON e2.person_id = g.person_id
   AND e2.ev_date > g.index_date AND e2.ev_date <= DATEADD(day,365,g.index_date)
WHERE g.trt_group IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY g.trt_group

## On the mechanism question (independent of the pending numbers)

The literature (IMPACT, ETHOS, KRONOS, FLAME) is directionally clear and worth stating regardless of what our EHR proportions show:

- **In frequent exacerbators, ICS-inclusive regimens (triple therapy) generally lower the exacerbation rate vs LABA/LAMA — but the benefit is concentrated in patients with high blood eosinophils** (roughly ≥300 cells/µL). Below ~100 cells/µL the benefit largely disappears and pneumonia risk dominates.
- **Immunologic rationale:** eosinophilic COPD exacerbations reflect **type-2 (Th2/ILC2, IL-4/IL-5/IL-13)** airway inflammation, which is corticosteroid-responsive — ICS suppress eosinophil recruitment/survival and type-2 cytokine signaling. **Non-eosinophilic exacerbations** are predominantly **neutrophilic/Th1–Th17 (IL-8, IL-17), often bacterial/viral-driven and relatively corticosteroid-resistant**, and ICS in that setting mainly increases airway infection/pneumonia risk (blunted innate defense) without cutting exacerbations. LABA/LAMA reduce exacerbations chiefly through **bronchodilation and reduced air trapping**, a non-immunologic mechanism.

So the expected finding is that **ICS-inclusive shows the lower 12-month exacerbation-visit proportion in the frequent-exacerbator group overall, driven by the eosinophilic subset** — which is exactly what I'd want to confirm (ideally stratified by eosinophil count) once the database is responsive.
